messages.text: Is it quiet enough to run in my office?

**Yes, absolutely** — it's designed for exactly that.

- **~40–45 dB** — roughly the level of a quiet room or a laptop fan. Tolerable on a desk all day.
- One large front fan moving air slowly across an adequate heatsink — no screaming tiny fan.
- **0.5 kg, ~20 × 11 × 5.8 cm** — palm-sized, sits on its included stand angled toward you.
- The spring-mounted heatsink keeps all four BM1370 chips cool (~57 °C at full load), so the fan never has to work hard.

One honest note: **not silent** — you'll notice it in a dead-quiet room, but most people find it disappears into normal office background noise.
What stops it from overheating or dying?

Good question — several layers work together:

**1. Spring-mounted heatsink**
Presses evenly on all four BM1370 chips — no one "hot corner" die cooking while the others stay cool.

**2. Custom BSB airflow shroud**
Ducts cold air directly onto the voltage regulators (VRMs) — the part that **usually dies first** on cheaper miners. Most boards leave VRMs completely bare. Result: VRMs run ~54 °C at full load vs. 70 °C+ on lesser boards.

**3. XT30 power connector + thicker PCB**
Rev 5 used an 8 A barrel jack that sagged and melted under load. Rev 6.1 swaps in a **15 A XT30 connector** on a thicker copper PCB — no voltage sag, no cooked connector running 24/7.

**4. Onboard F1 fuse**
A sacrificial blade fuse sits right on the board next to the XT30. If there's a power spike, **the fuse blows — not your miner.** Cheaper units skip this entirely.

**5. 350 W MEANWELL PSU (included)**
Industrial-grade supply loafing at ~30% load feeding a ~100 W miner — runs cool and quiet, never straining.

Bottom line: the parts that typically kill small miners — hot VRMs, weak power input, no protection — are all specifically addressed here.
